newsitem.title: USA: CBOT July soybeans surge late on stocks, El Nino.
newsitem.headline: CBOT July soybeans surge late on stocks, El Nino.

text.p: Worries over tight supplies of U.S. soybeans pushed the July contract to sharply higher gains on Tuesday at the close, traders said.
"Everybody is still nervous over supply, and the El Nino stories aren't helping either," said one floor trader.
On Tuesday, an official with the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration said El Nino-related droughts were likely in some countries.
"In Australia, we anticipate the dryness we're seeing is going to develop into a full-scale drought," Ants Leetma, director of NOAA said Tuesday.

Additionally, private consultant Sparks Cos. of Memphis, Tenn was said to issue forecasts showing 1996/97 (Aug/Sept) soybean ending stocks at a razor-thin 115 million and 1997/98 (Aug/Sept) ending stocks at 123 million bushels, traders said.
Current supplies have already dwindled to 20-year lows, and Sparks' new crop forecast is far below the government's latest of 240 million bushels.
A blast of buying coming from the options pit was also said to boost July futures late, pit sources said.
July soybeans settled up 14-1/2 cents per bushel higher at $8.53, and other months ended up six to 10-1/4 cents.
Some traders however, downplayed the significance of the Sparks estimate and said the market was due for a bounce.
"I don't think the Sparks number had much to do with this," said Vic Lespinasse, floor trader with Dean Witter. "It's oversold, and we were due for a bounce."
Nearly ideal growing conditions in the U.S. Midwest were expected to limit gains this week, traders said.
Most forecasters see warm temperatures and periodic rains for the week, traders said.
"Everything is green and lush," said one floor trader.
On the day, Lind-Waldock bought three million bushels July and Refco Inc bought 3.5 million November and sold two million July, traders said. Term Commodities sold 1.5 million November.
In options trade, Cargill Investor Services bought 600 July $8.50 calls and sold 200 July $8.25 calls. Lind-Waldock bought 500 July $8.25 calls, pit traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 60,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 48,616 contracts.
